TITLE: Safran Q3 2026: no upgrade, the de-rating overshoots
QUOTE: That’s what we see, and this is why we are fully confident and basically the end of the year is somehow ballistic now. We are very confident in 2027, and we are still confident in 2028.
QUOTE_WHO: Olivier Andriès, Chief Executive Officer, Q3 2026 revenue call, 23 October 2026
H_P1: What the quarter means for the investment case
C1_TITLE: SAF: Q3 2026 revenue and 2026 guidance vs. consensus
C1_SUB: % vs. consensus · Q3: company-compiled consensus · FY26: guidance midpoints vs. consensus per analyst first takes
BASE_CASE: We stay positive on Safran and would build positions on this weakness. The earnings path we underwrite is intact: 2026 operating income of EUR 6.4bn to EUR 6.5bn reached without the LEAP-1B profit release, which now adds to 2027, and a 2028 target of EUR 7bn to EUR 7.5bn that management said in July may be revisited. The debate has moved to 2027 aftermarket growth, now framed as CFM56 price plus LEAP volume. The catalyst is 2027 guidance at the full-year results in February. Near term, jet fuel and French tax headlines can keep the shares under pressure.
UPSIDE: 2027 guidance in February implying operating income growth above 10%, helped by the LEAP-1B profit release; Q4 spare parts up in the mid to high 20s as guided; advance payments on India’s 114 Rafale order; a good price for the cabin business.
DOWNSIDE: CFM56 retirements running above the 3% baseline assumed for 2027, or shop visits falling below the 2,400 plateau; the French surtax kept at the 2026 rate, worth EUR 500m or more in 2027; capex above 6% of sales eroding cash conversion.
H_A1: Results: the aftermarket still carries the group
H_A2: Outlook: 2026 held, 2027 rests on price and LEAP
H_C2: Valuation: the multiple has done the adjusting
C2_TITLE: SAF: share price vs. consensus earnings and valuation
C2_SUB: Weekly, Sep 2005 to 23 Oct 2026 · Bloomberg BEst 12m-forward EPS · 40-week MA · Log scale · Last price: 23 October, intraday, after the release
SOURCE_LINE: Source: Syz Research, Bloomberg, Safran Q3 2026 revenue call of 23 October 2026, Safran H1 2026 earnings call of 28 July 2026, company-compiled consensus, analyst research notes of 23 October 2026

TAKEAWAYS.label: In line
TAKEAWAYS.text: Q3 revenue rose 13.4% organically to EUR 9.0bn; Q4 spare parts are guided up mid to high 20s.

TAKEAWAYS.label: No raise
TAKEAWAYS.text: Targets were confirmed, not raised: the EUR 6.45bn operating income midpoint sits 2.1% below consensus.

TAKEAWAYS.label: Watch
TAKEAWAYS.text: 2027 CFM56 aftermarket growth rests on price alone, while capex rises above 6% of sales.

TAKEAWAYS.label: Valuation
TAKEAWAYS.text: The shares fell 6.2% to 27.0x forward earnings, below their five-year average of 30.0x.

P1_PARAGRAPH: The quarter was sound, and the 2026 targets held even though a LEAP-1B maintenance-contract profit release in the low hundreds of millions of euros slipped into 2027. Investors wanted more: no upgrade, a CFM56 aftermarket that grows only through price in 2027, capital spending stepping up to above 6% of sales and a French surtax extended into 2027. Management answered the fear of shrinking workscopes directly: they should stay at today’s high level.
C1_COMMENT: Group revenue matched the company-compiled consensus within 0.1% and Equipment & Defense beat by 2.5% on guided bombs, optronics, navigation and missile seekers. Aircraft Interiors missed by 1.3%, as seat certification still paces deliveries. The two bars on the right carry the message: confirmed targets sit about 2% below consensus, so estimates edge down rather than up into the full-year results.
A1_PARAGRAPHS: Revenue reached EUR 9.0bn, up 14.7% reported and 13.4% organically, in line with the EUR 8.99bn company-compiled consensus; currency added 1.1 points and scope was neutral. Propulsion revenue rose 13% organically to EUR 4.6bn. Civil engine spare parts grew 17% in dollars, below the 24% over nine months because of a strong Q3 2025 base, but up 4% on the second quarter, helped by CFM56 and LEAP pricing. Services grew 19%, led by LEAP maintenance contracts, while military engines declined on the Rafale delivery schedule. LEAP deliveries reached 535, up 5%, and 1,565 over nine months, up 26%, on track for more than 2,100 this year.

Equipment & Defense revenue rose 16% organically to EUR 3.6bn, ahead of the EUR 3.53bn expected, on strong demand for Hammer guided bombs, optronics, inertial navigation and missile seekers. Aircraft Interiors grew 6% to EUR 751m, against EUR 761m expected; certification still paces seat deliveries and may push some into early 2027. Safran has launched the sale of its cabin business, about EUR 2bn of revenue with positive operating profit and cash flow. Airbus selected the SkyNaute inertial navigation system for the A220, Safran’s entry into commercial navigation. No profit figures are reported at the third quarter.
A2_PARAGRAPH: Safran confirmed its 2026 targets: revenue growth in the mid-teens, recurring operating income of EUR 6.4bn to EUR 6.5bn and free cash flow of EUR 4.7bn to EUR 4.9bn, despite moving a LEAP-1B profit release in the low hundreds of millions of euros to 2027. Spare parts should rise by the mid to high 20s in Q4 and the mid-20s for the year. For 2027, management expects CFM56 shop visits flat at 2,400 and workscopes stable at today’s high level, so growth comes from price and LEAP. Capex will exceed 6% of sales every year, and the draft 2027 budget extends the surtax, at a cost of around EUR 400m.
C2_COMMENT: Over 12 months the share price fell 7.9% while consensus forward EPS rose 27.9%: earnings kept rising and the multiple absorbed the whole correction. At 27.0x forward earnings the stock trades 27% above its 21.3x average since 2005, but below its one-year average of 31.7x and its five-year average of 30.0x. The multiple has fallen from 34.9x at the record high of EUR 363.6 on 12 August, and the price sits 10% below its 40-week average of EUR 317. Even a 5% cut to consensus EPS at today’s price would leave the multiple at 28.5x, still below its five-year average.
